sources.title: Baroness Ashton of Upholland: current membership, party, committees and ministerial dates
sources.findings: Read Parliament member 2500 career record. Current House membership begins 2 August 1999; current Labour affiliation begins 10 November 2023 after a non-affiliated period from 14 October 2008. European Affairs Committee membership begins 31 January 2024. UK Engagement with Space Committee chairmanship ran 30 January–20 October 2025 and is not current. Education under-secretary work began June 2001, Constitutional Affairs September 2004, Justice May 2007, and Lords leadership/Lord President June 2007. Correct the raw draft’s Ministry of Justice date of 2004. Do not confuse this woman with Lord Ashton of Hyde, member 4247.

sources.title: 9 July 2026: The Space Economy committee report debate
sources.findings: Read the opening of Hansard’s 9 July 2026 space-economy report debate. Ashton moved the motion and introduced the committee report, credited members, clerks and advisers, and sought action on recommendations. This is a record of actual parliamentary participation, not merely an event announcement. No forecast satellite counts, GDP dependence estimates or claimed economic effects are independently validated or reproduced.

sources.title: 16 May 2012 honorary-fellowship citation: 1977 social-sciences degree and public career
sources.findings: Read all three pages of the Royal Holloway citation dated 16 May 2012. It confirms a 1977 social-sciences degree at Bedford College, 1999 life peerage and October 2008 succession to Mandelson as the first British woman on the European Commission. The final paragraph confers an Honorary Fellowship, not an honorary doctorate. Correct that distinction explicitly. Prefer the primary document’s social-sciences description over inconsistent secondary economics/sociology labels. November 2009 political selection is distinct from the 1 December legal mandate.

sources.title: Institutional history: 2010 decision, 2011 launch and high-representative mandates
sources.findings: Read EEAS institutional history. Lisbon Treaty created the institutional framework, the Council adopted the service’s organisational decision on 26 July 2010 following Ashton’s proposal and parliamentary involvement, and the service formally launched on 1 January 2011. The page separately records Solana’s earlier common-foreign-and-security-policy office and Ashton’s expanded 1 December 2009–31 October 2014 mandate, followed by Mogherini from 1 November. Avoid portraying Ashton as the EU’s first ever foreign-policy representative or sole institutional creator.

sources.title: EUCO 1/09: appointment text and mandate ending 31 October 2014
sources.findings: Read EUCO 1/09 appointment text in the Council register. Its recital records the initial 1 December 2009 appointment, and article 1 sets the following Commission-period mandate through 31 October 2014. This copy has blank adoption/signature lines; its 2 December cover date is not substituted for the start of office. Cross-check actual mandate dates against the EEAS chronology.

sources.publisher: European Union / reproduced by Iran Watch
sources.title: 24 November 2013 Ashton–Zarif joint statement: first-step measures and further negotiations
sources.findings: Read Iran Watch’s reproduction of the 24 November 2013 Ashton–Zarif joint statement. It identifies the six powers, Geneva talks, a first six-month phase of reciprocal measures and the shared intention to negotiate a final comprehensive settlement. Preserve its status as an interim Joint Plan of Action. The French foreign-ministry PDF redirected to a homepage and a Spanish defence-hosted copy timed out; neither is claimed as read in full.

sources.title: 14 July 2015 Mogherini–Zarif joint statement on the JCPOA
sources.findings: Read the EEAS-hosted 14 July 2015 Mogherini–Zarif statement. It identifies the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, collective negotiating effort, six powers and the Iranian side. This is a later agreement concluded after Ashton’s high-representative term, not another name or date for the November 2013 interim arrangement. Predictions about lasting peace or guaranteed outcomes are not adopted as observed facts.

sources.title: 25 April 2013 ministerial statement: 19 April Serbia–Kosovo agreement
sources.findings: Read the 25 April 2013 Hansard ministerial statement’s enlargement and foreign-affairs sections. It explicitly dates the Serbia–Kosovo agreement to 19 April and describes the EU-facilitated dialogue and Ashton’s role. This contemporaneous record corrects the transposed 2103 year printed in the later scrutiny report. Praise by ministers is attributed to those ministers, not treated as an independent measure of impact.

sources.publisher: House of Commons European Scrutiny Committee
sources.title: 21 July 2015: EU-facilitated dialogue, the 2013 agreement and continuing normalisation
sources.findings: Read the July 2015 European Scrutiny report’s background to Serbia–Kosovo normalisation. It identifies Ashton’s chairing of ten rounds, agreement by both prime ministers, and continuing implementation/normalisation needs. The page’s 19 April 2103 is a typographical error, corrected from the contemporary April 2013 record and the surrounding chronology. Do not label the agreement a complete settlement of every dispute or universal recognition of Kosovo.

sources.title: 23 April 2023: Garter appointment and 1956 birth year
sources.findings: Read the Royal Household’s 23 April 2023 Garter announcement. It confirms appointment as a Lady Companion and birth year 1956. Its compressed ministerial dates and broad peace-settlement wording are not adopted over detailed parliamentary records. The exact 20 March birthday appeared in indexed European Parliament and PBS material, but the direct pages were inaccessible, so this dossier keeps year precision.

sources.title: 19 June 2023: Garter Day investiture and service
sources.findings: Read the Royal Household’s 19 June 2023 Garter Day account. Ashton and Patten are named among new members invested at Windsor. Distinguish the June ceremony from the April appointment announcement; do not move the legal appointment date to June.

sources.publisher: IAEA / copy hosted by Security Council Report
sources.title: INFCIRC/855, 27 November 2013: circulation of the 24 November Joint Plan of Action
sources.findings: Read the machine-readable cover page of IAEA INFCIRC/855 hosted by Security Council Report. It confirms a 27 November 2013 communication by the EU High Representative for the six powers, circulating the agreement reached with Iran on 24 November. Only the cover text was extracted; scanned attachment pages were not visually inspected and no detailed nuclear limits are claimed from them.

sources.title: Current profile: strategic supporter and adviser; previous diplomatic career
sources.findings: Read Chatham House’s biography and current role heading. It labels Ashton a strategic supporter and adviser to Chatham House, not a Chatham House distinguished fellow; the fellowship in the biography belongs to the Wilson Center. Retain Parliament as authority for current legislative roles. The profile’s Nobel-nominee claim is not independently confirmed or reproduced, and its June Garter wording refers to the ceremony rather than the April announcement.

sources.title: Spoken contributions: 2026 space-economy and European-affairs debates
sources.findings: Read Parliament’s spoken-contributions index: records include 26 February, 11 March, 21 May and 9 July 2026. Its latest listed debate is the July space-economy report discussion, corroborated by the transcript. These records establish activity on recorded dates, not continuous physical presence or health status through the November verification cutoff.
